**Clinical Impression:**  
✅ **Left Leg Pain Secondary to Left Legg-Calvé-Perthes Disease (LCPD)**  
— Radiographic confirmation: AP and lateral left hip X-ray demonstrates flattening and fragmentation of the left femoral head.  
— Classic presentation: Knee-predominant pain ("referred gonalgia"), limping, activity avoidance, and absence of local knee signs or structural abnormalities on exam and advanced knee imaging.  

**Key Diagnostic Insights:**  
• Knee pain in children must prompt evaluation of the hip — especially when knee exam and imaging are unrevealing.  
• LCPD typically affects children aged 4–10 years; onset is often insidious, with intermittent limp and poorly localized pain.
